name: lookup_move
description: Read a move's trigger, stat, and every outcome band by id or name. Read it before deciding whether a move applies.

name: roll_move
description: Ask the player to roll a move for their character: 2d6 plus the stat the move uses, plus any condition penalty. For a move that rolls one of several stats, give the stat. Add a modifier for what the story gives, such as +1 for a Friend or -1 from a Condition. Write the prompt the player sees, in the GM's voice, inviting the roll. The player presses the roll button; the engine resolves the band and applies its effects.

prompt.description: What the GM says to the player to invite the roll. The player sees this text.

character.description: The name of the player character who rolls.

modifier.description: A situational modifier from the story. Use 0 when none applies.

stat.description: The stat to roll with, for a move that does not name one.

spell.description: The spell being cast, when the move is a spell.

player_input.details: The engine adds the move's stat and any condition penalty.

name: adjust_counter
description: Change a character's Stress, Faculty Favor, or Peer Standing. Use a negative change to spend or clear and a positive one to add. Do not use it for Year or Advancements; those change through the school year and the Advancement page.

character.description: The name of the player character.

change.description: How much to add (positive) or remove (negative).

name: take_advancement
description: Spend one Advancement point on a stat, a spell, a subject, or a talent. For the player character, use the option the player has stated; the character sheet is where the player makes the choice. For a stat, use stat; for a feature, use feature.

character.description: The name of the player character.

stat.description: The stat to raise, for the stat option.

feature.description: The feature to learn, for the spell, subject, or talent option.

name: end_period
description: End a school week or the school year. A week clears weekly reactions such as Natural Gift. The school year raises every living player character's Year, grants four Advancement points, clears Stress, logs the College Cup's final totals, and resets the cup. Call a week when a week of story time has passed, and the year only when the year actually ends.

name: set_relation
description: Make someone a player character's Friend or Rival, or end that relation. Use it only at the end of a session, as the rules require.

character.description: The name of the player character.

other.description: The name of the person, player or non-player, they are linked to.

added.description: true to make them this relation, false to end it.

name: start_project
description: Begin a long effort and track its points toward a target: a class challenge, spell research, potion research, or enchantment research. The kind and goal are free text; the target is how many points of work it needs. Advance it with advance_project as time, favours, and rolls are spent.

name.description: The project's name, unique among projects.

kind.description: What sort of effort it is, such as class, spell research, potion research, or enchantment research.

target.description: How many progress points it needs.

force.description: Set true to replace a project of the same name.

name: advance_project
description: Add progress to a class challenge or a research effort. Record in the note what the time, favour, or roll bought. The project completes when progress reaches its target.

name: abandon_project
description: Give up a class challenge or research effort.

name: list_projects
description: List every class challenge and research effort with its progress, notes, and whether it is complete or abandoned.

patch.description: Move the campaign clock forward. Use it when time passes in the fiction: days, parts of the day (morning, afternoon, night; eight hours each), or hours within a part. The result says when a new day begins and lists places not visited for a while. Do not advance time again for a rest, and do not use it to skip a scene the players are in.

Record a rest for the party. 'moments' is a short break of one hour, such as tea and a sit-down; 'night' is a full night's rest, which runs until morning; 'downtime' is a week of rest, and it ends conditions such as Burnout. The rest moves the clock itself, so do not also advance_time for the same time. Set interrupted when something breaks the rest, and then it counts as moments only.

length.description: How long the rest lasts: 'moments', 'night', or 'downtime'.

reason.description: What the party was doing, such as 'slept in the dormitory'.

patch.description: Look up the party's recent rests and each character's last full rest.

Find goods for sale by words in their name, category, or description. Every word in the query must appear. Each item gives its price in silver, size, and description. Use these prices when a character buys with buy_item.

query.description: Words to look for, such as 'parchment', 'reagents', or 'lantern'.

patch.description: Buy an object a character keeps: the character pays silver and the item goes into their pack. A catalogue item (see search_marketplace) costs its listed price, so leave price out. For anything else, give both a price you set from similar catalogue items and the item's size. Use buy_service for a room, meal, passage, toll, or other service that is not carried. There is no credit: a purchase is refused if the character lacks the silver or the room.

price.description: Silver to pay. Only for items not in the catalogue; a catalogue item's price must match its listing if given.

patch.description: Buy a service for one or more characters: a room, meal, passage, toll, bribe, or anything else that is not carried away. A listed service uses its listed price and effect, so leave price out. For any other service, give a price you set from similar services. The first character named pays for the whole service. A service never adds an inventory item.

price.description: The price in silver for a service the marketplace does not list. Leave it out for a listed service.
